page.lede: Skyloom before and after the Living World graphics pass: the same poses, sun, weather, traffic and lens on both sides, rendered on the RTX 5080. Drag across a frame to compare, or switch it to Before or After.

flags.name: Sky
items: LIVING_CLOUDS
Cloud light from the sky at the deck, ground-lit bases, multiple scattering
FAR_CLOUDS
The cloud deck continues past 22 km to the horizon, soft and shaded
SKY_TRAILS
Contrails that persist and spread behind cruising jets and your own
NIGHT_SKY
The Milky Way where it really is, fading under city skyglow; twinkling stars; a moon with maria
FILM_GRADE
Fine film grain after the grade
RAIN_OVERLAY
Rain and snow streaks stay visible against the sky
CIRRUS, LIGHT_SHAFTS, LENS_FLARE
Off: they did not hold up on the RTX 5080

flags.name: Aircraft
items: AIRFRAME_DETAIL
Panel lines and rivets, glass canopies with a pilot, prop discs, running lights that read by day
VAPOR_FX
Transonic vapour cone, over-wing vapour under load, wingtip vortices

flags.name: Ground
items: NIGHT_LIGHTS
NASA Black Marble city light on a street-lamp pattern beyond the generated city
GROUND_MIST
Mist that pools in valleys at dawn and dusk and in humid air

flags.name: Menus and HUD
items: MENU_GLASS
One glass design for Pause, Settings and Credits
TITLE_MOTION
Wordmark, card art, an entrance sequence and a lit Continue
FLIGHT_INSTRUMENTS
Speed and altitude tapes, a heading scale and a flight-path marker
HANGAR_STAGE
Studio light, a reflective floor, door haze, eased camera moves and a turntable

page.revert: Every change is one flag at the end of lib/fly/fly-constants.js. Add ?flags=-NAME to the address to see the previous look for one page load, or ?flags=NAME to try one that ships off.
runlist: Fly a hard turn low over the sea in a fighter: the tip vortices and wing vapour should look strong but believable.
Cruise at FL350 at night over the US East Coast: city light as street grids with dark country between.
At 1,500 ft at night over a city, judge the far city: from low down it is brighter than the ground beneath you, and at dusk it reads pale.
Fly at golden hour toward the sun: backlit clouds should be warm grey, not blue.
Open the hangar on Medium or above and watch the frame rate: the reflective floor draws the hangar twice.
Check the title wordmark: the thread through "loom" can read as a strikethrough.
page.method: Captured with scripts/capture-graphics-pass.cjs against production builds of ebfb6ab and the final tree, sun, weather, governor, lens and animation clock pinned, synthetic traffic. Every look flag that ships on was also checked in motion on the same GPU: a still camera must change no more than with the flag off, and a burst of flying frames must not crawl or pop. These are look evidence, not frame-rate measurements.
